Nothing here blocks the PR.

I found one correctness issue and one question. Neither blocks.

### 1. A dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink fails the new unit

- **File:** `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service`
- **Added line:** `ExecStart=/bin/cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json %h/.claude/settings.json`
- **Reason:** bug
- **Blocks:** no
- **Description:** GNU `cp` will not write through a dangling destination symlink. It stops with "not writing through dangling symlink" and exits 1, unless `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set. The unit's comment says `cp` was chosen to write through a dotfiles symlink, but that only works when the link's target already exists. `claude-pre-approval@merge` handles this case: it resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the target file as `{}`. The new unit doesn't.
- **Trigger:** `/home/dev` is a persistent volume (ADR 0012). It can hold a `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink whose target file is missing, for example after the dotfiles checkout was moved, deleted or not yet cloned. The target file is missing but its parent directory exists.
- **Path:** `templates/coder/main.tf@coder_agent.main.startup_script` (`systemctl --user start agent-services.target`) → `agent-services.target@Wants` → `claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` (`cp` fails) → `claude-pre-approval.service`, which still runs because `Before=` only sets ordering → `claude-pre-approval@merge`, which creates the target as `{}` and adds `enableAllProjectMcpServers` when trust is on.
- **Outcome:** `claude-default-settings.service` ends up failed and no Claude default settings are applied. Remote control starts with a `settings.json` that holds only `{"enableAllProjectMcpServers": true}`, or no file at all when trust is off. The startup script and the target don't report a failure, so the user doesn't see that the defaults are missing.
- **Fix:** resolve the link and create the target the same way `merge` does, for example `ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'f=$$(readlink -f %h/.claude/settings.json) && cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$$f"'`. Add a smoke case with a dangling link.

### 2. Question: is the different `attribution.commit` intended?

- **File:** `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.json`
- **Added line:** `"commit": "Built with AI",`
- **Reason:** bug (question only, no wrong outcome claimed)
- **Blocks:** no
- **Description:** The image's default settings otherwise copy `.claude/settings.json`, where `attribution.commit` is `""`. The image instead gives every workspace commit a "Built with AI" trailer, and the PR description doesn't mention it. Its `enabledPlugins` also lacks the repo's `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official`. If both differences are meant, nothing needs to change. If not, align them with the repo's settings.

### Ruled out
- **Ordering:** `Before=` on pre-approval and remote control, plus the target's implicit `After=` on the units it `Wants=`, means pre-approval adds its key after the copy. Smoke lines 89–94 would catch a wrong order.
- **Repeat starts:** with oneshot and `RemainAfterExit` it runs once per target start, and `PartOf` reruns it only when the target stops or restarts.
- **Ownership and mode:** the unit runs as dev and a new file gets 0644. It writes no secrets.
- **Smoke assertions:** they test what they claim, including that dev's own `model: "smoke"` is overwritten through the symlink.
- **ADR 0016 ("nothing is ever revoked"):** the overwrite would drop `enableAllProjectMcpServers` when trust is off. This can't happen in practice because the trust parameter is `mutable = false`.

I couldn't check offline whether `worktree.baseRef: "fresh"` is a valid key for the Claude Code version in the image, so I didn't raise it.

**Dismissed findings:** none.

CONFIRM — With a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink, GNU `cp` refuses to write through it and exits 1. `claude-default-settings.service` fails, but `agent-services.target` only `Wants=` it and the `Before=` ordering doesn't block anything. Remote control therefore starts without the defaults. The one caveat is that `claude-pre-approval` writes `~/.claude/settings.json` only when `CLAUDE_PREAPPROVE_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true`. It then creates the missing target via `readlink -f`. The finding's claim that it creates the target file holds only in that case, but the outcome holds either way.

DROP — The divergence is real (`attribution.commit` is `"Built with AI"` in the image and `""` in `.claude/settings.json`). But the value is a deliberate-looking custom string, and the image is a separate artifact from the repo's own settings. The claim cites no quoted rule and no input that produces a wrong result, so it is speculation rather than a defect.

review.body: I found no blocking issues. The title and description match the change. One non-blocking inline note: the defaults are not applied when `~/.claude/settings.json` is a dangling symlink.

comments.body:
A dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink makes this unit fail, so no defaults get applied. This is likely on a long-lived home volume, for example when the dotfiles checkout moved or does not have the file yet.

GNU `cp` will not write through a dangling destination symlink (`not writing through dangling symlink`, exit 1). `agent-services.target` only `Wants=` this unit, and `Before=` only orders it, so `claude-pre-approval` and `claude-remote-control` start anyway. Remote control then runs without the Claude default settings, and nothing visible reports it. `claude-pre-approval` already handles this case by resolving the link with `readlink -f` before writing.

Suggested fix: resolve the link the same way here, for example
`ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$$(readlink -f %h/.claude/settings.json)"'`
and add a smoke case with a dangling link.
